thread.title: Sixth Circuit affirms dismissal of lawsuit challenging Michigan reproductive rights amendment
thread.title_full: Sixth Circuit affirms dismissal of lawsuit challenging Michigan reproductive rights amendment

author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Sixth Circuit affirms dismissal of lawsuit challenging Michigan reproductive rights amendment
text:
The United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit affirmed on May 27 the dismissal of a lawsuit filed by Right to Life of Michigan and other anti-abortion plaintiffs seeking to overturn Michigan’s constitutional right to reproductive freedom. The court found that the plaintiffs did not have sufficient standing to sue Attorney General Dana Nessel, Governor Gretchen Whitmer, and Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson.
Attorney General Dana Nessel said, “From the start, this lawsuit was a procedurally flawed, meritless, and politically motivated attack on reproductive rights that Michigan voters overwhelmingly supported. I am relieved that the Court has once again rightly rejected this unfounded challenge. Although a loud faction remains determined to undermine bodily autonomy, the Michigan Constitution guarantees that decisions about your health belong to you. My office will continue to defend the reproductive freedom of Michiganders.”
Governor Gretchen Whitmer said, “Every Michigander deserves the right to make their own decisions about their own bodies. I’m proud of this decision, which protects Proposal 3 and affirms the fundamental right to reproductive freedom in our Constitution. In Michigan, we’ll always fight like hell for your rights.”
Following the U.S. Supreme Court’s 2022 decision overturning Roe v. Wade, abortion regulation authority shifted back to individual states. In Michigan, this led voters in November 2022 to pass Proposal 3 amending the state constitution with Article 1, Section 28—enshrining a fundamental right to reproductive freedom and preventing enforcement of an older law criminalizing most abortions.
Right to Life of Michigan and other opponents filed a federal lawsuit in November 2023 aiming to invalidate Article 1, Section 28 after Proposal 3’s passage. The Attorney General and other state officials moved for dismissal in January 2024; plaintiffs amended their complaint but defendants argued it remained flawed. The U.S. District Court dismissed all claims due to lack of standing among all fifteen plaintiffs; some appealed but were unsuccessful, as affirmed by yesterday’s Sixth Circuit opinion.

In Michigan, we’ll always fight like hell for your rights.” Following the U.S. Supreme Court’s 2022 decision overturning Roe v. Wade, abortion regulation authority shifted back to individual states.
